Message ArchitectureLink

Message PartRequired StandardApproved UseBlocked Drift
Subject lineSpecific, calm, and traceable to the commercial packet or response action.Reference Atlantic Foods, garlic offer, proforma review, response due, or packet follow-up.Do not use urgency language that implies crisis, allocation pressure, or shipment movement.
OpeningProfessional acknowledgment of the review item and current packet context.Confirm the packet, offer, specification, or response window without overstating commitment.Do not imply relationship familiarity is a substitute for proof.
Commercial statementPrecise summary of what is being reviewed and why the response matters.State pricing validity, product specification, response request, and payment-structure dependency.Do not treat high-confidence opportunity as booked revenue or approved release.
Action requestOne clear buyer action with a due point and owner expectation.Request receipt confirmation, commercial review, approval or rejection, and payment-structure confirmation where applicable.Do not ask for vague comfort, informal agreement, or partial approval that could be mistaken for commitment.
Deadline languageFirm, neutral, and tied to validity, pricing, or release-control consequences.Explain that stale response may require pricing or release revalidation.Do not threaten, pressure, or suggest automatic release after silence.
Escalation languageControlled and evidence-based.Escalate through response SLA, communication control, pricing governance, and founder review when timing weakens.Do not improvise new concessions, revised terms, or movement promises inside reminder language.
